t: that exists. Exists in reality (the expression "yesh sham" is in the manner of the Arabic idiom).
the First Being. This is God (below 1:5), whose existence precedes all existence. This precedence is both in time and in causation, as will be explained.
but from the truth of His existence. From the very true existence of the First Being.
And if it were to enter the mind that He does not exist, etc.. If it were conceivable that the First Being does not exist, it would be impossible to conceive of any existence at all.

And if it were to enter the mind that nothing exists besides Him. If one entertains the thought that nothing else exists besides Him, the matter would have no bearing on the existence of the First Being.

Therefore His truth is not like the truth of any of them. God's true existence is unlike anything else, for all things depend on Him and have no existence without Him, and He alone is truth in an absolute sense.

There is none besides Him, etc.. This expression should be understood not as a denial of other existences, but as a denial that the perfect value of truth (of an ever-existing being) applies to any other being whose existence can cease and is not eternal like the existence of the Creator.
the One who turns the sphere. This is the definition, according to the science of that time, of the primary force that sets everything in motion (see below, chapter 3).
with a power that has no end or limit. That never ends.
without a hand or a body. That is, without any physical means of any kind.
And knowing this. That there is a First Being, and the relation between the truth of His existence and the truth of the existence of all other beings.
I am the Lord your God. To make known that the Lord who speaks to Israel is God. This is not merely a declaration of existence but a commandment to know and believe in Him.
and denies the fundamental principle. The principal foundation of religion.
for this is the great principle on which everything depends. That the belief in the unity of God is the principle and basis of all the commandments of the Torah.
that His unity is not like the unity of any of the units. That His definition as one is not similar to the definition of the concept "one" in any sense or context found in created beings.
not one like a species that includes many individuals. That one species includes different individuals.
nor one like a body that is divided into parts and extremities. That a single body is divided into the limbs that compose it.

If there were many gods, they would be bodies and physical forms, etc.. The proof of God's unity stems from the very definition that He is not a body, for the necessary result of positing multiple deities is that they are limited to bodies, since the difference between things of identical essence is expressed only through different bodies and their events.

And if the Creator were a body and physical form, He would have an end and limit, etc.. And from the fact that His power has no end, it follows that He Himself has no end, and thus the possibility of multiple deities is ruled out.
And knowing this. Regarding the unity of God.
and a body cannot be in two places. That every body is subject to the limitations of space.
and it is stated: "for you did not see any image". That even at the time of God's revelation to Israel at Mount Sinai, no image of any form was seen.
"To whom will you liken Me, that I should be equal?". To whom or to what can God be likened at all? He has no form, and therefore cannot be compared to anything else.
and if He were a body, He would be like other bodies. If He had the properties that every body has (length, width, and the like), He could be likened and compared to other bodies.
If so. If God indeed has no body, how are the verses that refer to His body to be explained?
"and under His feet". Of God, at the time of the revelation at the Covenant of Sinai: "like a work of sapphire brick and like the very heavens for clarity."
"written by the finger of God". The Tablets of Testimony that were given to Moses at Sinai.
according to the understanding of human beings. In accordance with the way humans perceive and think.
who know only bodies. All their knowledge is of things having physical properties.
figures of speech. Images and metaphors.
"If I sharpen My flashing sword". If I sharpen the blade of My sword. These are the words of God at the end of the Song of Ha'azinu.
All of it is a metaphor. Every physical image mentioned in the Torah is not a literal description but a metaphor for His actions and His revelation.
Proof of this. That all the physical descriptions of God are only metaphors.
"His garment was like white snow". His garment was like white snow.
"with crimsoned garments from Bozrah". When He returned from the city of Bozrah, His garments were red.
at the sea. At the splitting of the Red Sea.
like a mighty man waging war. As it is said in the Song at the Sea: "The Lord is a man of war" (Exodus 15:3).

and at Sinai. When Moses went up Mount Sinai again alone after the sin of the golden calf, and the Holy One, blessed be He, revealed to him the order of the Thirteen Attributes of Mercy. The Sages taught that the Holy One, blessed be He, wrapped Himself like a prayer leader and showed him the order of prayer.
to say that He has no form or image. For He is revealed in different ways, and not one of them is a description of reality but a metaphor.
And the truth of the matter. The true nature of the matter.
What is this, etc.. If God has no form at all, what did Moses mean when he asked Him, after the sin of the calf, to show him His glory?

He sought to know, etc.. Moses' intent was also by way of metaphor: that he should perceive God's existence as clearly as the form and appearance of another person are clear in the mind of someone who has seen him, to the point that he finds in him features that distinguish him from other people.

And the Holy One, blessed be He, answered him, etc.. God replied that everything a person grasps with his mind is based on the fact that a person can fully understand only physical, material things, and therefore it is impossible that he grasp with his mind the true nature and existence of God as they truly are.
And the Holy One, blessed be He, informed him. Moses.

until he grasped of the truth of His existence something that distinguished the Holy One, blessed be He, in his mind from all other beings, etc.. Although He did not reveal to Moses the positive knowledge of God's existence (which is not attainable by human beings at all), he nevertheless attained in his mind a complete recognition by way of negation, that is, the essential difference between God's existence and everything else. Thus he attained a very lofty level of comprehension, but by way of negation alone.
that none of the incidents of the body occur to Him. None of the characteristics of physical objects can apply to Him.
neither joining nor separation. It is impossible to join Him to another body or to divide Him into smaller parts.
neither place nor measure. He does not occupy or exist in any place in space, nor does He have a measure.
neither ascent nor descent. Which are movement in space.
neither right nor left, nor front nor back. Which are concepts that belong only to a body.
and He does not exist in time. The dimension of time does not apply to Him.
like the life of a living body. These are characteristics found only in the bodies of living creatures.
foolishness. Stupidity.
awakening. Waking, rousing from sleep.
laughter. Laughter.
the back of the neck. The rear side, which symbolizes separation.
joining. Connection (Commentary on the Mishnah, introduction to Perek Chelek).
All these matters and similar ones. All the expressions in which these characteristics are attributed to God.
are all metaphors and figures of speech. As above, halachah 9.
And so it says. Similarly, Scripture itself testifies that these characteristics do not apply to God Himself.
"Is it Me that they provoke to anger?". The sinful Israelites in the time of Jeremiah: do they truly provoke God to anger?
"I, the Lord, have not changed". There is no concept of change with regard to God.
And if He were, etc.. Thus any human trait, such as anger and joy, is impossible with regard to God.
the lowly darkened ones. The coarse, material bodies.
"who dwell in houses of clay, whose foundation is in the dust". The language of the Book of Job (4:19): human beings whose spirit dwells within a material body, formed of dust (see Genesis 2:7).
that has no measure or end. That nothing can be compared to it, and it is infinite.
he recoils backward. He draws back, out of the realization of his own insignificance relative to the Creator.
dark. Dark and material.

as David said: "When I see Your heavens". "the work of Your fingers, the moon and the stars which You have established," and then the thought arose in him, "What is man...?" - what is man and what is his worth?
And according to these matters, etc.. Because contemplating God's works leads to love and awe of Him (see also below 4:12).

As the Sages said regarding love, etc.. Regarding the juxtaposition of the verses "You shall love the Lord your God... And these words that I command you today shall be upon your heart" (Deuteronomy 6:5-6), the Sages said that the way to reach love of God is to place "these words" upon your heart, "for through this you will recognize the One who spoke and the world came into being, and cleave to His ways" (Sifrei Deuteronomy, section 33). Similarly, understanding the works of creation can bring to love of God.

And according to these matters I will explain great principles, etc.. Below, in chapters 3-4, Maimonides gives a scientific description of the structure of the world, which he calls "Ma'aseh Bereshit" (the Account of Creation) (below 4:10). For the various approaches to this description by Maimonides, see the Appendices: "The scientific description of the world in Hilchot Yesodei HaTorah," p. 715.

creations composed of matter and form. Matter (golem) is the substance itself, which has no properties, and form is the totality of properties in the substance (weight, color, shape, and all other properties). According to this worldview, form is an entity in its own right, even though it is usually attached to matter.
and they come into being and pass away constantly. They are created and also perish at all times.

creations composed of matter and form but that do not change, etc.. Although they too have a basis of matter (golem) and properties (form), their essence does not change, and exists forever without change.

and their matter is not like other matter, nor is their form like other forms. According to this view, the stars are made of a special substance (a "fifth element") that is unlike the matter of the beings of our world. And even their form has properties that do not exist in other things in the world.
creations of form without any matter at all. Beings that are not material at all and are only "forms" - abstract, spiritual entities that are not joined to any matter.
forms separate from one another. That the angels are forms without matter, but they are forms different from one another (see below 2:5).
And what is this, etc.. If the angels lack matter and body, how can one explain their description in the verses as made of fire, or as having wings?
and by way of a riddle. A metaphor and an image (see below 7:3).

to say that it is not a body and not heavy, etc.. This metaphor comes to say that angels are not a body, like fire, and lack the properties of a body such as physical weight (and the wings hint at this).
as it is stated: "For the Lord your God is a consuming fire". Just as God is said to be fire, which is also by way of metaphor (see above 1:9).
And how are the forms distinguished from one another, etc.. If the forms have no material existence, what is the difference between them (see above 1:5)?
that they are not equal in their existence, etc.. They differ from one another in their properties, in the essence of that form.
and it exists by His power. That the relationships between them are causal, with the higher being the cause of what is beneath it.
"for one higher than the high watches". This means that the angels are not identical to one another but are at different levels.
"and they shall know that a prophet was among them". The words of God to Ezekiel, that although at first they will not believe him, in the end they will know that his words are true.
beneath its level. That every form is below the level of the preceding form.
is not a level of place. The difference between them is not one of physical position, with one situated above the other.
and as we say of the cause that it is above the effect. Just as the cause of a thing (the "cause") is treated as though it is situated above the thing that results from it (the "effect").

The different names of the angels, etc.. The various names given to the types of angels were determined according to their level: the highest rank is the Chayot HaKodesh (holy living creatures), and the lowest is the Ishim.
above which there is none, etc.. That it is the highest level.
Therefore it is stated in the prophecy. Ezekiel 1:26.

They are the angels who speak... whose level is close to the level of human knowledge. Their rank and spiritual comprehension is only slightly higher than the comprehension of human beings (and a person upon whom the spirit of prophecy rests reaches in his mind the level and spiritual comprehension of the Ishim - below 7:1).
not according to His greatness. Of the Creator, for His greatness is infinite and unattainable.
even the first level, etc.. Even the highest rank, the Chayot HaKodesh, has no power to comprehend the Creator as He is.
the tenth level also knows, etc.. Even it knows the Creator in a way that human beings cannot understand, because they are limited in their comprehension due to their material component.
and none of them know the Creator as He knows Himself. For only He alone can comprehend Himself.
from the first form. The Chayot HaKodesh.
at the center of the earth. In the middle, in the interior of the earth.
everything exists by the power of His truth. As explained above, 1:1-3.

And since He knows Himself, etc.. Since all existing things depend on and derive from "the truth of His existence," in a certain sense He includes them all. And in knowing Himself He knows everything that exists in the world.
and He does not know with a knowledge that is external to Him, etc.. That in the Creator there is no separate essence of "knowledge" with which He knows, as there is in created beings.

for if He lived with a life and knew with a knowledge, there would be many gods. For those attributes (life and knowledge), if they were separate, would have to be at the level of divinity, and it would turn out that there are many deities.
One in every respect, etc.. As explained above, that His unity is unlike any in any other existence - a completely perfect unity.
and He is the known. For He knows things by knowing Himself, and so He is both the knower and the known.
and He is the knowledge. Which is not a separate essence in itself, as stated.
Therefore we say, "As Pharaoh lives," etc.. In the construct form, meaning the life of Pharaoh. Likewise "as your soul lives" - the life of your soul.

and we do not say "the life of the Lord" but "the Lord lives". With regard to God, one cannot speak of the life of God, for it is in complete unity with His essence. Rather, we say "chai Hashem" (the Lord lives), which is an adjective, similar to the expression "the living God."
in this matter. Of the existence of the Creator and His knowledge, and His relationship to existence and to created beings, and the angels and their intellectual level and the human intellect.

only to one person alone. To a single individual privately and not to teach several people together, out of concern that the matters will not be properly understood by one of them and the teacher will not be able to clarify it (see below 4:11).
wise and understanding of his own accord. Who understands matters by himself, and there is no need to explain to him; a hint suffices.
they transmit to him the chapter headings. They teach him the main points.
a trace. A little.
to bear them. To understand them.
the hidden things of the world. The concealed (hidden) matters of existence.
"for your clothing" - that is, for you alone. Like your garments, which you wear and do not share with others.
matters that are like honey and milk. Pleasant and tasty matters.
"shall be under your tongue". You shall enjoy them alone (and see below 4:13).
and the spheres. According to Maimonides, the spheres are real entities, like a physical sphere formed as a shell of the globe. The heavenly bodies revolve within the spheres and by means of them.
the one closest to it. The closest to the earth.
a star. In our day it is called Mercury (Kokhav Chamah).
in which is the sun. The sun.

a sphere that revolves every day from east to west. That is, in the outermost sphere there is no particular star or heavenly body, but it rotates constantly and continuously (from east to west, and again and again), and by the power of this sphere's constant rotation the other spheres attached to it rotate.
pure and clear like glass and sapphire. Completely transparent.

is divided into many spheres, etc.. The multiplicity of spheres helps explain the movements of the planets, which do not appear to move in one direction and moreover change their direction of movement.
like the layers of onions. Composed of several layers, like the structure of an onion.
there is no empty space between them. There is no gap of void or space between one sphere and the next; they are adjacent to one another.
colors. Colors.
like the appearance of sky-blue (tekhelet). The shade of the sky.
is only for the appearance to the eye. That the blue color is what our eyes perceive from the light of the sun, but this is not the color of the spheres.
and the earth is suspended in the middle. At the center of that system of spheres, with all of them moving around it (see Hilchot Kiddush HaChodesh 11:13-14).
that are fixed in them. In the large sphere.
a small sphere that does not encompass, fixed in the large encompassing sphere. And therefore their motion varies.
the measure of their revolution. The extent of their motion.
and this is the science of calculating the seasons and the constellations. See Hilchot Kiddush HaChodesh 11:2.
and the Greek sages composed many books on it. On whose words the matters written here rely (see Hilchot Kiddush HaChodesh 17:24).

after a form that appears, etc.. The stars (fixed stars) set in the eighth sphere are arranged in groups with imaginary shapes such as a ram, a bull, etc., and according to these shapes names were given to the twelve parts of the ninth sphere.
and these are the constellations (mazalot). Each of the groups of stars is aligned with the position of the sun in one of the solar months (and see Hilchot Kiddush HaChodesh 9:3).
the ninth sphere itself has neither division nor form. For it contains no star itself, but only turns the spheres beneath it.

but through the grouping of the stars in the eighth sphere, etc.. The grouping of the large stars found in the eighth sphere created shapes after which the parts of the ninth sphere were called by the names of the constellations.

and these twelve forms were aligned with those parts only at the time of the Flood. Those twelve groups of stars were aligned at the time of the Flood exactly with the corresponding parts of the ninth sphere (for example, the group of the ram was then exactly above the part of the firmament belonging to the month of April).
they have already rotated a little. That these stars also move, and have changed their position in the sky as a result of a shift from west to east (see Hilchot Kiddush HaChodesh 12:2).
slowly. Sluggishly.
and the earth is about forty times larger than the moon. This refers to their volume, not their diameter.
and the sun is about one hundred and seventy times larger than the earth. These statements are based on an ancient estimate of the proportions of the earth and the sun.
are possessed of a soul, knowledge, and intellect, etc.. That they are not merely matter but have awareness and intellect.
below the sphere of the moon. In the space between the sphere of the moon and the globe of the earth.
one matter that is not like the matter of the spheres. A different substance, not identical to the substance of the spheres, which is the basic substance of the various materials of our world.
and He created four forms for this matter. These are the properties of the "four elements" from which our world is composed.
and they are not like the form of the spheres. The properties of the four elements are not like the substance of the spheres, which is a kind of "fifth element."
they do not possess a soul. Unlike the systems of stars and spheres.
a custom that it does not know, grasp, or be able to change. A fixed pattern of behavior; nature.
And this is what David said, etc.. David's words should not be explained as an appeal to the forces of nature to praise God, since they have no soul.
The meaning of the words "Praise Him, O sons of man, for His mighty acts which you see, in fire and hail, etc.". That these words express a heavenly might that is evident to human beings.
they are the elements of all created things beneath the firmament. The basic components of all substances.
its matter. The substance from which it is made.
composed of matter and form, etc.. As explained above, 2:3.
for their course to be from below, from the center of the earth, upward toward the firmament. That their nature is to rise from the center of the world upward.

for the middle of the firmament is the "below" beneath which there is nothing lower. For the firmament is shaped like a sphere, and its center point is the lowest place in relation to the circumference.
and their movement is not by their knowledge or will. The movement of the four elements does not stem from their will but from the nature of their creation.
and each of them changes at the time of mixing. The elemental substances that compose bodies are present in each of them in a different proportion.
and in the mixture there is not even one part that is fire by itself, etc.. The elemental substances exist (in pure form) only in their own places, and on earth there are mixtures of these elements.
cold and hot, moist and dry together. All the components, in varying proportions.
more heat is seen in them. They generate heat to a greater degree than other creatures.
in the end it separates, etc.. In the future it will disintegrate and return to its elements, for this is the nature of everything composite.
even gold and ruby. Which do not appear to be subject to the action of other substances.
and the ruby. An especially hard gemstone.
why was it said to man, "and to dust you shall return". Is he not destined to separate into all four elements?
and not everything that perishes, when it perishes, immediately returns to the four elements. To the primary elements.
they go around in a cycle. That all things in the world change and take on different properties after they are separated.
and is dissolved. Separated and disintegrated.
and this change will be in the revolution of the sphere. This change will occur as a result of the rotation of the sphere.
the tenth angel, which is the form called Ishim. Above, 2:7.
you never see matter without form or form without matter. In reality one does not see pure matter, and one does not discern pure form.
rather it is the human heart that divides, etc.. It is our perception that makes the distinction between matter itself and its form, but this is not apparent to the eye.
and bodies whose matter is simple. The spheres and the stars (above 2:3).
and the forms that have no matter. The angels (ibid.).
are known to the eye of the heart. In the understanding of every person.
as we know the Master of all without seeing with the eye. Just as God's existence is known without seeing Him.
the soul of all flesh is its form, which God gave it. The basic form of a person (not his physical structure) is called the soul.
and the additional knowledge found in a person's soul is the form of the person who is perfect in his knowledge. That is the form of a perfect human being.
and of this form it is said in the Torah. In describing God's decision on the sixth day of creation to create man.
a form that knows and grasps ideas that have no matter. The ability to know of the existence of entities that are not physical (above 2:3).
until he becomes like them. That he has the ability to resemble the angel in his mind (see below 7:1).
and it does not refer to this form that is visible to the eyes, etc.. The divine image in which man was created does not refer to a person's body, nor to the physical life force.
but rather the knowledge that is the form of the soul. The special intellectual faculty of man (and see further Hilchot Teshuvah 8:3).
Therefore one must be careful with the terms, so that you do not err. Do not confuse the meanings of "soul."
it will be learned from its context. It will be understood from the context in which sense of "soul" it is speaking.
from the power of the neshamah. It is the power that gives life to the body.
Therefore when the matter separates. At the time of death.
this form will not be cut off. The soul is not lost even after death (see Hilchot Teshuvah 8:3).
like a drop from a bucket. Like a drop of water from a full bucket (based on Isaiah 40:15).
for one does not expound even these matters in public. Lest they not be properly understood (and see also above 2:12).
only to one person. Private instruction.
they give him the chapter headings. The main points.
even if he does not understand it on his own. That it is not necessary for him to understand matters by himself; rather, it can be explained to him.
he increases love for the Omnipresent. Out of admiration for the wisdom of their creation (see also above 2:2, Hilchot Teshuvah 10:6).
and his flesh will yearn. He will long and desire.
when he compares himself, etc.. When he tries to place himself in relation to those exalted creations.
to one of the great holy bodies. Such as the spheres and the stars.
to one of the pure forms separate from matter. That are not essentially connected to any matter.

that in these five commandments. Enumerated at the beginning of Hilchot Yesodei HaTorah: to know that there is a God, that it should not enter one's mind that there is another god besides the Lord, to unify Him, to love Him, and to fear Him.

as they said: "Four entered the Pardes, etc.". In the aggadah of the Sages about the Sages of Israel who engaged in these hidden matters, some of whom were harmed because of this study (see Babylonian Talmud, Chagigah 14b).
to stroll in the Pardes. To walk about in it, that is, to contemplate these matters.
who has filled his belly with bread and meat. Satisfying eating of basic foods.
and the matter of Abaye and Rava is a small thing. An example of the discussions common in the Talmud, which are small in comparison to the subject of Ma'aseh Merkavah.

which are the great good that the Holy One, blessed be He, bestowed, etc.. That through the study of Torah and the proper fulfillment of the commandments one merits life in the World to Come (see Hilchot Teshuvah 9:2).
one with a broad heart and one with a narrow heart. Between one whose mind is suited to delve deeply and contemplate, and one who is not capable of this (see Hilchot Talmud Torah 1:12).
the sanctification of this great Name. The sanctification of the Name of the Holy One, blessed be He.
and forces. Compels.
he is liable for his life. He deserves punishment for causing his own death.
if his intent was only to make him transgress the commandments. That his entire intent is to cause Israel to transgress the commandments.
only one of the other commandments. Another commandment that is not one of the three severe commandments: idolatry, forbidden sexual relations, and murder.
When does this apply. That regarding the other commandments one must transgress and not be killed.
like Daniel. Who prayed in defiance of the decree of King Darius and was thrown into the lions' den (Daniel chapter 6).
Chananiah, Mishael, and Azariah. Who refused to bow to the image that Nebuchadnezzar set up and were thrown into the fiery furnace (Daniel chapter 3).
and like Rabbi Akiva and his colleagues. Who gave their lives for words of Torah and were slaughtered for it (Babylonian Talmud, Sanhedrin 110b).
for there is no level above their level. For their level is the highest level.

"Gather to Me My devoted ones, who made a covenant with Me by sacrifice". This is expounded as referring to the righteous of every generation who give their lives for their covenant with the Holy One, blessed be He.
as it is said of one who gives of his seed to Molech. Which is one of the types of idolatry (see Hilchot Avodah Zarah 6:3).
and from the oral tradition. The tradition of the Sages.
from everything. From all the other transgressions (see Hilchot Avodah Zarah 2:4).
one who worships it under duress is not liable to karet, etc.. That one who worships idols is liable to karet and death only if he worshiped willingly (see ibid. 3:1).

and regarding forbidden relations it says, etc.. From this verse, which is stated regarding a betrothed maiden who was raped, it can likewise be proven that one who commits a transgression under duress is not punished for it (and see also Hilchot Sanhedrin 20:2).
"and let us defile her". Let us have relations with her.
they singled him out for them. They requested a specific person.
like Sheba son of Bichri. Who incurred the death penalty because he rebelled against King David (II Samuel chapter 20).
but we do not instruct them to do so initially. That it is not proper to do so.
as they said regarding those under duress, etc.. That a person is permitted to transgress a prohibition in order not to die.
and are healed. And are cured.
"You shall love the Lord your God... even if He takes your soul". From here it follows that one may not worship idols even if he will be killed for refusing.
a coercer. A violent person.
a matter to which the mind inclines. A matter that is understood logically.
as it is said: "For as a man rises up, etc.". This verse, stated regarding a man who rapes a betrothed maiden, equates the act of forbidden relations with murder.
the way they are normally enjoyed. The usual manner of using them.
that we feed him on Yom Kippur. See also Hilchot Shevitat Asor 2:8.
a poultice. A bandage with ointment.
a compress. Food that is chewed and placed on the skin for healing purposes.
things that contain a bitter substance mixed with forbidden foods. See also Hilchot Ma'achalot Assurot 14:11.

except for kilayim of the vineyard and meat with milk, etc.. Because, unlike all the other prohibitions in the Torah, in which the prohibition is stated in terms of eating, in these two the prohibition is written in different language (see Hilchot Ma'achalot Assurot 14:10).
who set his eyes on a woman. Lusted after her.
even if she was unmarried. In which case there is no prohibited relation.
with contempt of soul. With scorn.

and therefore it is stated regarding a false oath, "and you shall profane the name of your God". That although it is not one of the three severe transgressions, it involves desecration of the Name (see also Hilchot Shevuot 12:1), and likewise any transgression done to spite.
like the restraint of Joseph the Righteous, etc.. Who refused the entreaties of Potiphar's wife to lie with her, saying: "How can I do this great evil and sin against God?" (Genesis 39:9).
crowned with tefillin. See Hilchot Tefillin 4:25.
provided that he does not go too far from people or become desolate. That he not behave in an extreme manner and as a result become distant from people (see Hilchot De'ot 3:1).
praise. Extol.
whisper behind him. Speak against him.
and does not pay the price of the purchase immediately. See also Hilchot De'ot 5:13.
immediately. At once.
he has. The ability to pay for it at that time.
buys on credit. Buys on account.
that he not engage excessively in laughter or in eating and drinking with the ignorant. See Hilchot De'ot 2:7, 5:2.
his speech with people is gentle. See also Hilchot De'ot 5:7.
and is insulted by them but does not insult them. See Hilchot Talmud Torah 7:13.
those who belittle him. Those who do not treat him respectfully.
faithfully. With integrity and fairness.
in hosting by the ignorant. Being a guest at the home of the ignorant.
or that which is written Alef, Dal, Nun, Yod. This is the manner in which the Ineffable Name is pronounced (Hilchot Tefillah 14:10; and see Hilchot Avodah Zarah 2:7).
Dal. The name of the letter dalet in the Arabic language.
any prefix attached to the Name before it. The introductory letters written before the Name.
Kaf, Mem. The names of the letters kaf and mem in the Arabic language.
lashes for rebelliousness. Lashes by rabbinic decree.
and there is no need to mention Yah. When one intended to write this name by itself.
he may not bathe, etc.. Lest the Name on his flesh be erased by the water.
nor stand in a place of filth. A place where there is excrement and the like, out of respect for the holiness of the Name (see Hilchot Keriat Shema 3:4).
a reed. A band made of rush.
searches. Looks for.
so that it not be a barrier. For a barrier invalidates immersion (see Hilchot Mikva'ot 1:12).

for they did not say to wrap it around him, etc.. The purpose of the covering is that he not stand naked before the Name of God, and therefore there is no need to tighten the reed; it is enough to wrap it around him.
one who demolishes even a single stone. See also Hilchot Beit HaBechirah 1:17.
sanctified wood. Wood that was consecrated to the Temple for its maintenance (Responsa of Maimonides, 160).
a heretic (min). One who denies the existence of the Creator and His unity (as detailed in Hilchot Teshuvah 3:7).
they burn it together with the Divine Names in it. The names of God written in it (see also Hilchot Tefillin 1:13).
and likewise worn-out holy writings. See also Hilchot Sefer Torah 10:3.

All the names mentioned regarding Abraham... regarding Lot, etc.. The word "Adonai" mentioned in the account of the arrival of the angels to Abraham (Genesis chapter 18) refers to the Holy One, blessed be He, whereas regarding Lot (ibid., chapter 19) this word refers to the angels and means "my lords."

All the names mentioned regarding Gibeah of Benjamin, etc.. The names mentioned in the Israelites' inquiry of God whether to go out to battle against the tribe of Benjamin (Judges chapter 20) refer to the Holy One, blessed be He, even though it seems that the answer given to them did not come true.
All the names mentioned regarding Micah are secular. The names mentioned in the account of Micah's idol (Judges chapters 17-18) refer to idolatry and not to the Holy One, blessed be He.

The names mentioned regarding Naboth are holy. In the false accusation that Ahab brought against him, "You have blessed God and the king" (I Kings 21:10, and also 21:13), and it does not refer to Ahab's idolatry.
All "Solomon" mentioned in the Song of Songs is holy. Because it alludes to the name of God.
and it is like the other appellations. That there is a prohibition against destroying them (above, halachah 8).
All "the king" mentioned in Daniel is secular. For they refer to King Nebuchadnezzar.
perfect in his body. Who has no physical blemish.
when he enters the Pardes. Delving into the fundamentals of religion: Ma'aseh Merkavah and Ma'aseh Bereshit (see above 4:13).
those who are distant. From understanding the minds of human beings.
who walk in the darkness of time. Who follow the enticements of passing time, who resemble blind people walking in the dark.
from the vanities of time and its schemes. The passing vanities, which with great cunning entice a person.
bound beneath the Throne, etc.. Attached and constantly contemplating the forms of the angels and their levels (which reach down to beneath the Throne of Glory - above 2:7).
and contemplates the wisdom of the Holy One, blessed be He. Contemplates the works and creations of the Holy One, blessed be He, in which His wisdom is evident (above 2:2).
from the first form to the center of the earth. Beginning with the most spiritual form (the Chayot HaKodesh) up to the most material reality (the center of the earth).

his soul will mingle with the level of the angels called Ishim. The level of his intellectual comprehension will rise until it resembles the comprehension of the lowest level of angels, who are the ones who speak with the prophets (above 2:7).
on the day after a deep sleep falls upon them. A kind of numbing of the senses and weakening of the body at the time of the prophetic vision.
and their thoughts are confused. Their senses become confused.
as it is said regarding Abraham, etc.. At the time of the prophetic vision of the Covenant between the Parts, when a deep sleep and great dread fell upon him.
and as it is said regarding Daniel. When he saw one of his prophetic visions.
"and my comeliness was turned in me into corruption, and I retained no strength". My face was disfigured, and no strength remained in me.
and immediately the interpretation of the allegory is engraved in his heart. Already at the time he sees the allegory, he knows its interpretation.
the ladder that our forefather Jacob saw, etc.. In his dream at Beth-El (Genesis 28:10-22), which was an allegory for the nations that would enslave Israel.
the creatures that Ezekiel saw. In the Account of the Chariot (see Ezekiel chapter 1), which are an allegory for the revelation of God.
and the steaming pot and the almond rod that Jeremiah saw. At the beginning of his prophecy (Jeremiah 1:11-14), which were allegories for the destruction that would come upon Judah.

and the scroll that Ezekiel saw. That God showed him a large scroll written on both sides, and afterward he was commanded to eat it (Ezekiel 2:9-3:3), and this is a general allegory for his prophecy and the relationship to it.
and the ephah that Zechariah saw. Who saw an ephah (a large measuring vessel) with a woman inside it being carried to the land of Shinar (Zechariah 5:5-11).
they state only the interpretation. Most of the words of the prophets, which do not describe a particular allegory and vision that they saw, but only the content of the thing symbolized.
they prophesy in allegory and by way of a riddle. And not clearly, unlike Moses our teacher (below 7:6).
they focus their minds. And contemplate those concepts described above.
sluggishness. Heaviness of body and heart.
the sons of the prophets. Those who wish to prophesy (see the next halachah).
they walk in the way of prophecy until they prophesy. They train and prepare themselves for prophecy.
So-and-so is growing. Is becoming great.
in a dream. During sleep at night.
in a vision. A vision by day, at a time when the senses and body are dulled (above, halachah 2).
all the prophets prophesy through an angel. Through an intermediary power between the prophet and the prophecy (see Guide for the Perplexed 1:37; 2:45).
therefore they see what they see in allegory and riddle. Not something clear and absolute but something that requires the prophet's interpretation.
face to face. Directly, without any intermediary between him and the prophecy.
clearly. Plainly.
they are frightened, alarmed, and overcome. They are filled with fear, as described above, halachah 2.
no prophets prophesy whenever they wish. Rather, they must focus their minds beforehand (above, halachah 4), and even so it is possible that they will not prophesy.

"Stand, and I will hear what the Lord commands concerning you". So Moses said to the men who wanted to know what their law was since they had not offered the Pesach offering because of their impurity.

as it is said. After the revelation at Mount Sinai, where all of Israel saw the revelation of God and heard His voice, and in this respect they were like prophets, like Moses our teacher (see below 8:1-2).
and the skin of his face shone. His face glowed and radiated, as a result of his speaking with the Divine Presence (see Exodus 34:29).
to give understanding. To teach them and add to their understanding.
a sign and a wonder. A miraculous act that proves his trustworthiness.
his peers. His contemporaries (like the meaning of the root "gil" in Arabic; and see Devarim Rabbah, Lieberman edition, 123; Ruth Rabbah 2:8).

as it is said: "to him you shall listen". These are the words of Moses, and the beginning of the verse: "A prophet from your midst, from your brethren, like me, the Lord your God will raise up for you," that is, he must be at a level worthy of prophecy ("like me").
and this is the sign: he has matters behind him. Another factor is hidden behind him, such as sorcery or sleight of hand.
we maintain him in his presumptive status. Since he is fit for prophecy, we assume that the sign he performed is genuine.
as we were commanded. See Hilchot Sanhedrin 20:1, 24:1; Hilchot Edut 3:4.
"The hidden things belong to the Lord our God". Things that are not revealed to human beings are not their responsibility but the responsibility of the Lord.
"and the Lord sees into the heart". And this is not the role of man.
a blemish. A flaw, a doubt.
by sorcery. By acts of witchcraft.
and drowned them. Sank them.
"It was not with our fathers that the Lord made this covenant". And the continuation: "but with us, we who are all here alive today."
as it is said. In God's words to Moses before the giving of the Torah.
those to whom he was sent. All of Israel.
they are the witnesses to his prophecy that it is true. For they saw for themselves that God speaks with Moses.
for they and he are one in the matter. There is no difference between Moses and Israel with regard to the truth of Moses' prophecy.

for each of them is a witness to his fellow that he speaks the truth, etc.. When a witness saw something together with his fellow, there is no need for him to bring proof that his fellow speaks the truth, for he himself saw the same thing, and thus his testimony about the event is also testimony to the trustworthiness of his fellow.
at the beginning of his prophecy. When He appeared to him at the burning bush and commanded him to take Israel out of Egypt.

at the time that He gave him the signs. So that he could prove to the Israelites that he was the prophet of God, and they are: turning the staff into a serpent, turning his hand leprous, and turning some of the water of the Nile into blood (see Exodus 4:1-9).
this is what the verse says. That the true sign that God sent him would be when they serve God at Mount Sinai (the giving of the Torah).

so too it is a commandment to listen to this prophet, whether the sign is true or by sorcery and trickery. Whether the sign is genuine or not, it is a commandment to listen to the prophet, for so Moses commanded in the Torah.
and sought to deny the prophecy of Moses our teacher. The Torah of Moses, its details and its commandments.
explicitly. Clearly.

so that we compare this sign to that sign. Because the trustworthiness of Moses does not derive from the signs he performed, there is no place at all to evaluate and compare the signs of this prophet with the signs of Moses.
as he heard. Moses our teacher.
for it is a commandment that stands forever and for all eternity. That the Torah is eternal (see Hilchot Teshuvah 3:8).
"It is not in heaven". That is, the Torah and its commandments no longer depend on revelation from heaven, such as through prophecy.
an interpretation that we did not hear from Moses. That contradicts the traditions we received as a law given to Moses at Sinai.
"God is not a man that He should lie". God is not like human beings, whose words are not eternal and may be false; rather, the validity of His word is eternal.
why does the Torah say, "I will raise up a prophet for them". What is the purpose of the prophet?
to make a new law. To introduce new laws.
the last of them. Malachi, the last of the prophets.
in matters of discretion. Matters that do not concern positive commandments or prohibitions.
who transgressed his own words. That he himself does not heed what he received in prophecy.
and one who suppresses his prophecy. Who keeps it to himself and does not publicize it to the public.
whom we know to be a prophet. Whose trustworthiness has been proven (see below 10:2).
as a temporary measure. On a temporary basis (compare Hilchot Mamrim 2:4).
who offered a burnt offering outside. When he wanted to prove that the prophets of Baal were false prophets, he built an altar on Mount Carmel and offered a sacrifice on it (see I Kings 18:20-40).

and Jerusalem was chosen. And at the time of this incident the Temple in Jerusalem had already been built, and it was forbidden to offer sacrifices on private altars (see Hilchot Beit HaBechirah 1:3; Hilchot Ma'aseh HaKorbanot chapter 18).

"lest you offer your burnt offerings in every place". The beginning of the verse: "Take heed to yourself lest you offer...," and the continuation: "but in the place that the Lord will choose... there you shall offer your burnt offerings."
from oral tradition. From tradition.
in one of the laws of the Torah. Whose details are in dispute among the Sages.
spoke rebellion. Words of incitement and falsehood.
and the sign and wonder came to pass. Of the prophet who incites to worship idols and proves it with signs.

for he comes to deny the prophecy of Moses. For Moses himself commanded that anyone who claims that idols should be worshiped and backs it with a sign and wonder is a false prophet and an inciter and is subject to the death penalty (see Hilchot Avodah Zarah 5:1). And Moses did not make an exception that it would be permitted in the case of a temporary directive, and it is already known that one who denies the prophecy of Moses is certainly a false prophet (above, 8:3).
and his words will be believed. And his prophecy will come true.

"How shall we know the word". "that the Lord has not spoken." That is, how will we know whether this prophet's words are indeed the words of God? And Scripture's answer: "when a prophet speaks in the name of the Lord and the thing does not occur or come to pass, that is the thing that the Lord has not spoken."
one fit for prophecy. See above 7:1.
in a mission. In a mandate.
fell. Did not come true.
he will be trustworthy in our eyes. In the meantime, until he is tested many times and established as a prophet.
the soothsayers and diviners. Those who claim to foresee the future in various ways (see Hilchot Avodah Zarah 11:6-9).
"Let them stand now and save you, etc.". The words of the prophet who mocks those who trust in stargazers and fortune-tellers, for they cannot tell all that will happen in the future.
"who frustrates the omens of the false prophets and makes diviners mad". The Holy One, blessed be He, frustrates the signs of fortune-tellers and confounds their minds.
like straw mixed with a little grain. Like the chaff of grain mixed with a little good grain, for most of their words are nonsense and some are true.
like grain that has no straw at all. All of it is words of truth.
and they lie. Their words do not come true.
who makes his son and daughter pass through fire. And the continuation of the verse says, "a soothsayer, an augur, a sorcerer."
"For these nations". "listen to soothsayers and diviners." But the people of Israel are not so, rather: "A prophet from your midst... the Lord will raise up for you."
like Saul, who had lost something. The donkeys that his father Kish had lost, and he went to ask Samuel (I Samuel 9:1-11).
not that he should make a different law. As above, 9:1-2.
and He relented concerning the evil. Reverses His decision to do harm.
like the people of Nineveh. Jonah prophesied that it would be destroyed, but by the merit of their repentance this decree was nullified (Jonah chapter 3).
that it delayed for them. Repentance postponed the punishment.
like Hezekiah. Who fell ill, and Isaiah prophesied to him that he would die, and by the merit of his repentance God gave him another fifteen years until his death (Isaiah chapter 38).
even conditionally. As a possibility and not as a definite promise.

that only by words of good is the prophet tested. Only in a prophecy about a good thing that will happen can the prophet be tested, for if it does not happen as he said there is no explanation other than that he is a false prophet.
to Hananiah son of Azzur. A false prophet in the days of Jeremiah.
when Jeremiah was prophesying evil. That the Temple and Jerusalem would be destroyed.
and Hananiah good. That not only would there be no destruction, but even the exile that had already been exiled to Babylonia (the exile of Jeconiah) would return in two years (Jeremiah chapter 28).
this is no proof. For any prophecy of evil may not come true if they repent.
and was walking in the ways of prophecy. In the way of conduct that leads to prophecy (see above 7:7).
and it is forbidden to test him. To examine his words and ask him for a sign.
"as you tested at Massah". There the people complained to Moses that there was no water (Exodus 17:1-7).
when they said, "Is the Lord among us or not?". That is, they doubted Moses our teacher, whether his leadership of them was in accordance with God.
